Subject: Performance SLO / Benchmark methodology — follow up and next steps

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance SLOs and the benchmark exchange: 

What we heard (your targets):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 150ms for short-chat responses (<= 128 tokens); p90 streaming token latency target ~40ms/token.
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state ~100 requests/s, ability to absorb spikes to 250 reqs/s; expected concurrency ~200 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: must support real-time token streaming to browser clients with consistent token-rate throughput (20-30 tokens/sec per stream).
- Measurement reproducibility: you want artifact-free, repeatable runs (seeded prompts, synthetic user traces, and environment notes).

Agreed next steps:
1) We shared two artifacts as attachments: edgefin-benchmark-promptset-v1.jsonl (sample prompts / user journeys) and redwood-benchmark-guidelines.pdf (measurement definitions + harness instructions).
2) Dev will follow up with the exact harness configuration (concurrency distribution, warmup rules, what we measure client vs server-side).
3) You (EdgeFin) will confirm any adjustments to targets and whether we should include some of your real traces (anonymized) vs synthetic only.
4) Run a first reproducible pass next week (we propose Wed/Thu) and then schedule a 30-min results review.

Questions for you:
- Are the p95 / throughput numbers above still accurate? We want final confirmation before we kick off the run.
- Any IP/network constraints (eg. allowlist IPs) for the benchmark runner?

If that looks good I’ll schedule the harness run and send a calendar invite for a 30-min sync to review results.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: p95 target is important for us, but we currently expect to accept up to 200ms p95 for some complex templates. Can we run the baseline at 150ms and also include a 200ms threshold for the heavy prompts?
- Throughput: the 100 reqs/s steady number is correct; we also want to validate a burst to 300 reqs/s for 60s as part of the resilience test.
- Streaming: we’ll validate token-rate (25 tokens/sec) and also want to confirm whether your harness measures server-side token emit time or end-to-end time to client (including network).
- IP allowlist: yes — we’ll need the runner IPs to allow in our test environment.

We’re happy to start with your attached promptset; if needed we’ll provide an anonymized trace later. For scheduling, Thu next week (May 27) morning PT works for our infra team.

Thanks Evan — quick technical clarifications and the measurement definitions we use so everyone is aligned: 

1) Latency definitions
- p95/p50/p90: measured at the Redwood server-side ingress that returns the final chunk for non-streaming responses. For streaming, we report per-token emit latency (server-side) and end-to-end latency which includes websocket push time to a test client.
- Tokenization: we include model tokenization time in the server-side latency measurement.

2) Throughput & concurrency
- Steady-state req/s is measured over a 5-minute window after a 2-minute warmup. Spikes are run as separate stress tests (we’ll run the 300 reqs/s burst for 60s as requested).
- Concurrency: we simulate concurrent streams with a Poisson arrival process to approximate real-world traffic — details in the attached guidelines.

3) Reproducibility & harness
- We provide a deterministic harness (bench-harness open-source repo link below) and a seedable promptset (attached). Each run records environment metadata (image versions, GPUs, kernel args, quantization flags). We’ll share a run artifact bundle with logs, perf counters, and a reproducible run script.

4) Security / network
- For IP allowlisting, here are the runner IPs: 3.120.45.22, 3.120.45.23 (we can use your ephemeral runners if you prefer). We’ll also run with synthetic data by default; if you supply anonymized traces we’ll treat them as customer owned and scrub identifiable fields.

5) Measurement outputs we’ll deliver
- CSV summary with p50/p90/p95 latencies, per-token latency distribution for streaming, throughput over time, tail-latency traces, and artifacts (logs + CPU/GPU telemetry).

Quick note on heavy prompts: we’ll tag prompts in the promptset as "light/medium/heavy" and report metrics per class so you can see the 150ms vs 200ms behavior.

Command-line example (bench-harness):
./run_bench --promptset edgefin-benchmark-promptset-v1.jsonl --concurrency 200 --target-reqs 100 --burst 300:60 --seed 42 --output results/edgefin-run-20260527

Let me know if you want us to run from Redwood-managed runners or your infra. If Redwood-managed, we’ll need allowlist done before the run.
